title: What are you doing this weekend?
goal: Make plans and say what you want — while untangling three words often all translated as "want": 要, 想, and 打算.
bekal: tell apart 要 (want, will), 想 (would like, be thinking of), and 打算 (plan to)
invite people and turn down invitations naturally

dialogs.title: 對話 — 週末計畫
dialogs.intro: Friday afternoon in the cafeteria. The three of them talk about weekend plans.

lines.speaker: 小美:
lines.id: What are you guys doing this weekend?

lines.speaker: 阿明:
lines.id: I'm going home to Tainan. It's my mom's birthday.
lines.literal: I — will — return — Tainan. I — mom — birth-day.

lines.speaker: 小美:
lines.id: What a good daughter! And you, Budi?

lines.speaker: 布迪:
lines.id: I'm thinking of going hiking, but I haven't decided yet.
lines.literal: I — would-like — go — climb-mountain, but — still — not — decide.

lines.speaker: 小美:
lines.id: Hiking's great! How about Elephant Mountain?

lines.speaker: 布迪:
lines.text: [象山|Xiàngshān][難|nán][爬|pá][嗎|ma]？[我|Wǒ][很久|hěn jiǔ][沒|méi][運動|yùndòng][了|le]。
lines.id: Is Elephant Mountain hard to climb? I haven't exercised in ages.
lines.literal: elephant-mountain — hard — climb — (question)? I — very-long — not — exercise — (change).

lines.speaker: 小美:
lines.id: Not at all! You're up in half an hour.
lines.literal: not — will — (softener)! half — hour — just — arrive — (change).

lines.speaker: 布迪:
lines.id: So do you want to come along?

lines.speaker: 小美:
lines.text: [好啊|Hǎo a]！[我|Wǒ][打算|dǎsuàn][傍晚|bàngwǎn][去|qù]，[可以|kěyǐ][看|kàn][夜景|yèjǐng]。
lines.id: Sure! I'm planning to go around dusk, so we can see the night view.
lines.literal: good — (softener)! I — plan — dusk — go, can — see — night-view.

lines.speaker: 布迪:
lines.id: Awesome! What time shall we meet?

lines.speaker: 小美:
lines.text: [四點|Sì diǎn][半|bàn][在|zài][象山|Xiàngshān][捷運站|jiéyùn zhàn][出口|chūkǒu][二號|èr hào]。
lines.id: Four thirty at Exit 2 of Xiangshan MRT station.
lines.literal: four — o'clock — half — at — Xiangshan — MRT — station — exit-mouth — two — number.

lines.speaker: 阿明:
lines.id: I'm so jealous! I'm coming next time too.
lines.literal: really — envy! below — time — I — also — will — go.

lines.speaker: 布迪:
lines.text: [記得|Jìde][帶|dài][水|shuǐ]。[我|Wǒ][不想|bù xiǎng][在|zài][山上|shān shàng][渴死|kěsǐ]。
lines.id: Remember to bring water. I don't want to die of thirst on the mountain.
lines.literal: remember — bring — water. I — not — would-like — at — mountain — on — thirsty-die.

lines.speaker: 小美:
lines.text: [放心|Fàngxīn][啦|la]！[山下|Shān xià][就|jiù][有|yǒu][小七|Xiǎo Qī]！
lines.id: Relax! There's a 7-Eleven right at the foot of the mountain!
lines.literal: let-go-heart — (softener)! mountain — below — just — have — little-seven!

notes: **孝順 (devotion to one's parents) is a value still very much alive in Taiwan.** Calling someone 孝順 is high praise, and going home for a parent's birthday is seen as normal, even for working adults.
**象山 (Elephant Mountain) is Taipei's most famous hike** — twenty minutes from downtown by 捷運, and the view of 台北101 from its top is the Taipei photo you've probably seen most.

**很久沒…了 means "haven't… in a long time"**: 很久沒運動了, 很久沒見了 (long time no see). ⚠️ Note that 沒 and 了 appear together here — an exception to the rule in unit 11, because what 了 marks is the state of "it's been a long time", not the event itself.
**放心 ("let go of the heart") means "relax, don't worry"**, and its opposite 擔心 ("carry the heart") means to worry. A pair of expressions with very vivid images.
⚠️ **出口二號 — exit numbers are the standard way to set a meeting point in Taiwan.** Big 捷運 stations have up to eight exits far apart, so just saying "at the station" isn't enough.

grammars.title: ⚠️ 要, 想, 打算: three levels of certainty
body: English can use "want" for a vague wish and a firm decision alike. Mandarin separates the three by **how certain** the plan is.
after: ⚠️ **不要 and 不想 are very different and often confused.** *我不想去* = "I don't feel like going" (soft, about feelings). *我不要去* = "I won't go" (firm, almost a refusal). And **不要 before a verb means "don't"**: *不要吃！* (don't eat it!).
**Turn down an invitation gently: use 不想 or a reason, not 不要.** *我今天有點累，不想出門* is far softer than *我不要去*.

**想 also means "miss" and "think"**: *我想家* (I miss home), *我想一下* (let me think a moment). The three meanings are told apart by what follows: a verb → would like; a person or place → miss; nothing → think.

grammars.title: Inviting and responding to invitations
body: Invitations in Mandarin are almost always questions, because inviting with a command sounds pushy.

head: 中文
Pīnyīn
Meaning
Tone
rows: Do you want to come along?

after: ⚠️ **Turning down an invitation in Taiwan almost always follows the pattern "reason + alternative"**: *這個週末有事，下次好嗎？* Refusing without a reason or without offering another time comes across as cold.
**Agreeing with a bare 好 sounds reluctant.** Add a particle: 好啊！好啦！好喔！ — all three sound warm.

blocks.title: Three most typically Taiwanese pastimes
items: **唱歌 at KTV** — private-room karaoke, paid by the hour, with unlimited food and drinks. It's the number-one social activity for young Taiwanese.
**泡溫泉** — Taiwan is full of natural hot springs (北投, 烏來, 礁溪). ⚠️ Some baths require you to be naked and separate men and women; others use swimsuits. Ask first.
**逛夜市** — wandering a night market with no particular goal, nibbling a bit here and there. It's not shopping; it's an activity of its own.
**爬山** — Taiwan is a mountainous island, and hiking is a national hobby. Even within Taipei there are a dozen or so trails you can reach by 捷運.

blocks.text: ⚠️ **Use 隨便 with care.** It means "whatever", and said in a flat tone it can sound indifferent or even annoyed — exactly like "whatever" in English. The safe choice is **都可以** ("anything's fine"), which sounds friendly.

⚠️ **Mandarin uses both words of the pairs 因為…所以… and 如果…就…**, unlike English, where one is enough. *因為很累，所以我不去* — both are there. Dropping one isn't wrong, but using both sounds neater and is easier to follow.

items: What are you doing this weekend?
I'm going home to Tainan.
I'm thinking of going hiking.
Do you want to come along?
If it rains, I won't go.
Don't forget to bring an umbrella.
